text.title: UI Library Advanced Patterns Core Rules
text.summary: 7 testable rules on compound-component wiring through context, the dialog focus contract, inert background handling, CSF 3 story shape, and keyboard-driven play functions. Each is checkable against the component source and its stories file.

rule.statement: Compound APIs (`<Tabs><Tabs.List><Tabs.Trigger/>`) MUST share state through a context created by the root component. `React.Children.map` + `cloneElement` to inject props into children is rejected.

rationale.source: React composition patterns / Radix compound-component model

rule.rationale: `cloneElement` reaches only direct children, so the moment a consumer wraps a trigger in a layout `<div>` or renders the list through `.map()`, the injected props stop arriving. Nothing throws: the trigger renders and simply does not respond, and the consumer concludes the component is broken rather than that the nesting is.

rule.statement: The internal consumer hook MUST throw a named error when its context is `undefined` — e.g. `throw new Error('<Tabs.Trigger> must be rendered inside <Tabs>')` — rather than returning `null` or a default object.
rule.rationale: `createContext()` with no argument yields `undefined`, and a hook that tolerates it produces a component with no registered state: keyboard handlers no-op and ARIA ids point at nothing. The symptom appears at the far end of the interaction, so debugging starts at the event handler instead of at the misuse, which is one file away.

rule.statement: A modal dialog MUST satisfy all six: rendered through a portal to `document.body`; `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal="true"`; labelled via `aria-labelledby` pointing at a rendered title; focus moved into the dialog on open; Tab and Shift+Tab cycled within it; Escape closes and focus is restored to the element that opened it.

rationale.source: W3C WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide — Dialog (Modal) pattern

rule.rationale: Each omission has a distinct failure. Without focus restoration the keyboard user is returned to document start and has to re-traverse the page to get back to where they were. Without a trap, Tab walks into the background content that is visually covered but still in the tab order, so the user is typing into controls they cannot see.

rule.statement: While a modal is open, background content MUST be made non-interactive with the `inert` attribute (or `aria-hidden="true"` on the app root sibling), and body scroll MUST be locked with layout-shift compensation (`scrollbar-gutter: stable`, or `padding-right` equal to the measured scrollbar width).

rationale.source: HTML `inert` attribute + assistive-technology virtual cursor behaviour

rule.rationale: An overlay is paint only: without `inert`, the screen-reader virtual cursor and Tab both still reach the content behind it, so the dialog is modal visually and not at all semantically. Locking scroll with `overflow: hidden` alone removes the scrollbar, and on desktop the reclaimed width reflows the entire page — the visible jump every time a dialog opens.

rule.statement: Stories MUST use CSF 3: `const meta = { component: X } satisfies Meta<typeof X>`, `export default meta`, `type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>`, and each story exported as an object with `args`. `storiesOf` and CSF 2 function stories are rejected.

rationale.source: Storybook Component Story Format 3 / portable stories

rule.rationale: The object form is what `composeStories()` can re-hydrate outside Storybook — it applies `args`, decorators, loaders and `play` when the same story is imported into a Vitest or Jest test. A function story carries none of that metadata, so reusing it in a unit test silently drops the decorators and the test exercises a component that never renders that way in the app.

rule.statement: Every interactive pattern MUST have a `play` function using `userEvent` from `@storybook/test` (`storybook/test` in Storybook 9+) that drives it with `keyboard`/`tab` — Tab, Enter, Space, Escape, Arrow keys as the pattern requires — and asserts resulting focus and ARIA state, not only that a click changed the DOM.

rationale.source: Storybook interaction testing + WAI-ARIA APG keyboard interaction sections

rule.rationale: Pointer events bypass roving tabindex, focus traps and Escape handling entirely, because those are implemented in keydown handlers. A click-only test therefore passes on a dialog that traps nothing and a tablist where every tab is in the tab order — the exact defects the pattern exists to prevent.

rule.statement: Do NOT apply when (a) the library has no shipped primitives yet — run `ui-lib-basics` first, since compound APIs over unstable primitives churn twice; (b) the surface has no overlay, disclosure or composite widget (cards, static text, plain buttons only); (c) Radix, Headless UI or React Aria already provides the primitive — wrap and style it rather than re-implementing a focus trap, which is where hand-rolled dialogs fail.
rule.rationale: Focus management is the part of these patterns with the highest defect density and the least visibility in review. Re-implementing it to avoid one dependency trades a maintained, tested implementation for one whose bugs surface only for keyboard and screen-reader users, who rarely file reports.
